item.title: #Hacking Social Media: 7 Rules for a Happy & Productive Social Media Experience — Mon Oct 5, 1:00 PM — Bendale
item.description:
Digital Inclusion Week: October 4th, 2026 - October 10th, 2026 Keith McDonald, founder of the literacy AI project, shares his seven rules for having fun with social media. Following these rules allows audiences to gain control over algorithms and learn how to recognize and deal with the social pressures, bullying, and reputational implications of social media use. The presentation also includes how to identify and reduce security and privacy risks. This is a multi-media presentation featuring video clips, props, and group discussions, and it begins with an opening social media song icebreaker. Space is very limited. This program takes place during Digital Inclusion Week 2026
Source: Toronto Public Library — Teens

item.description: A hands-on workshop where participants will learn how 3D Printing works and use Tinkercad to explore 3D design basics. New to 3D Printing and Design? Class instruction includes: How to prepare a 3D design file for print How to use the equipment properly and safely Reviewing the rules and guidelines to using the 3D printer Followed by the introduction to printing, class participants will be given a hands-on workshop where they learn how to create simple 3D designed key chain and become familiar with design tools. Registration is required for this class. You can order free tickets by clicking the link below. item.title: Community Listening Session & Introduction to Civic Innovation — Mon Oct 5, 7:00 PM — Albert Campbell
item.description: What does civic innovation actually mean and what does it have to do with you? This opening session brings the community together to answer that question. We will introduce the Civix by Design program, explore what civic innovation looks like in real neighbourhoods, and most importantly, hear from you: what challenges in your community matter most? Your input shapes everything that follows. This program is part of TPL's Innovator in Residence series focused on civic innovation. From October 5 to November 28, join programs, workshops and one-on-one consultations led by technology strategist Ismail Mohamud to learn how technology can help you create positive change in your community. Learn more at tpl.ca/iir .
